events.subtitle: Serenades & Simple Songs — World Premiere of Sarah Kirkland Snider's Urge
events.factual_description: The National Symphony Orchestra presents Serenades & Simple Songs at Lisner Auditorium on Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 7:00 PM. Teddy Abrams conducts, with bass-baritone Will Liverman joining for the world premiere of Sarah Kirkland Snider's Urge, an NSO co-commission setting a new text by poet Tracy K. Smith. Snider's official work page identifies the commissioners as the National Symphony Orchestra, Boston Symphony Orchestra, and Aspen Music Festival and School, says the work was written for Liverman to mark the United States' 250th anniversary, and lists the NSO and Liverman as the premiere performers. The program also includes Stravinsky's Symphonies of Wind Instruments, Michael Tilson Thomas's Street Song, and Tchaikovsky's Serenade for Strings. The NSO lists a second performance of the same program at Lisner Auditorium on Saturday, November 14 at 8:00 PM.

en.why_it_matters: The reason to go is not simply an NSO program with a new piece tucked inside it. Sarah Kirkland Snider's Urge is being born here: a new orchestral work written for Will Liverman on a Tracy K. Smith text, co-commissioned for the country's 250th anniversary and placed between Stravinsky, Michael Tilson Thomas and Tchaikovsky. That combination makes the premiere a live document of contemporary American concert music rather than a routine repertory night.
en.trip_verdict: Make room for the Thursday premiere if you are in the DMV and want to hear a major new work at the moment it enters the repertoire. The Saturday repeat gives a useful fallback, so there is no need to turn the premiere into a regional trip or displace a genuinely one-chance-only date.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para ir no es simplemente que la NSO meta una obra nueva dentro de un programa. Urge, de Sarah Kirkland Snider, nace aquí: una obra orquestal escrita para Will Liverman sobre un texto de Tracy K. Smith, co-comisionada para los 250 años de Estados Unidos y colocada entre Stravinsky, Michael Tilson Thomas y Tchaikovsky. Esa combinación vuelve el estreno un documento vivo de la música de concierto estadounidense actual, no una noche rutinaria de repertorio.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio al estreno del jueves si estás en el DMV y te interesa escuchar una obra importante justo cuando entra al repertorio. La repetición del sábado funciona como muy buen plan B, así que no hace falta convertir el estreno en un viaje regional ni mover una fecha verdaderamente de una sola oportunidad.
